- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the 30-day horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently neutral or mildly negative; model fails to capture downward bias in low-sentiment periods.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays mean reversion, especially after sharp spikes — true prices revert more quickly than forecasted.
- High sentiment + recent price spike → model overreacts and forecasts higher prices for next period; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment > 0.10.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to underestimate true price decline — adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon.
- Model overfits recent high prices; if last 3–5 days are high, reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid “price momentum” bias.
- Sentiment > 0.10 and price > 80 → model often overestimates future price; apply downward correction of 3–8% for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often undercorrects — increase forecast by 1–3% to avoid “sentiment lag” bias.
